questions: Separate passive observation from active restart permissions and live-lease checks.
Check restart-loop protection, scheduler portability and deduplicated alerts.
decision: Keep watchdog observation separate from guarded restart actions, with generation-fenced leases, bounded restart budgets and deduplicated anomaly notifications.
code_observations: watchdogctl distinguishes status observation from a watch loop that writes a deduplication cache. keepalivectl is the separate active restart component.
The existing mechanisms inspect lease, runnable work and restart history; absence of a console message is not sufficient reason to start another runner.
implementation_steps: Specify an observation record with anomaly class, evidence timestamp and suggested action; never mutate task status or restart from passive status.
Require an owned stale/dead local runner, runnable work and restart allowance before keepalive launches. Respect quota pauses, explicit pause and missing credentials.
Deduplicate repeated anomalies and bound observation-cache growth. Keep operational scheduling outside the semantic task prompt.
Add scheduler examples with explicit user opt-in and platform-specific quoting. Do not install cron/Task Scheduler entries during ordinary implementation.
Record restart reasons and outcomes without retaining provider transcripts or secrets. Failed environment probes do not trigger capability escalation.
Distinguish silence, death, stale lease and restart eligibility; unknown liveness cannot authorize recovery.
Fence keepalive actions by runner generation and preserve explicit user pause/cancel state.
Bound restart frequency and deduplicate anomalies without feeding healthy status loops to an LLM.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Repeated status calls leave plan/job/process state unchanged.
A live lease prevents duplicate restart even if the job appears quiet.
Restart-loop limits and manual pause suppress repeated launches.
Quota-resume timing is observed without a busy loop or premature paid dispatch.
Windows/POSIX scheduler command generation is tested independently from actual registration.
A recycled PID cannot be killed or treated as the old runner.
Repeated failure reaches a restart-loop guard rather than consuming unlimited attempts.
User pause remains effective after watchdog and host restart.
A stale observer suggestion cannot restart a new runner generation.

alternatives.title: Watchdog auto-repairs everything
alternatives.risk: Unbounded side effects and restart loops
alternatives.tradeoff: Convenient appearance; Unbounded side effects and restart loops. Reject

alternatives.title: Read-only watchdog only
alternatives.tradeoff: Safe diagnosis; Needs operator restart. Keep as default observation

alternatives.title: Separate guarded keepalive
alternatives.tradeoff: Controlled recovery; Needs ownership and budgets. Recommended opt-in action

alternatives.title: LLM decides liveness/restart
alternatives.tradeoff: Flexible; Cannot reliably prove process ownership. Reject as authority

cost_model: Measure recovery delay and false restarts against polling/probe overhead. Healthy watchkeeping has zero model cost; optional diagnosis is bounded per novel anomaly.
unverified: No host scheduler was installed and no real provider was restarted in this research.
No operating-system scheduler was installed or run. The plan requires platform-specific deployment tests separately from pure state-machine fixtures.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Keep watchdog observation read-only and keepalive restart narrowly authorized, with bounded probes, leases and loop protection.
revision_delta: The revision treats observed inactivity, confirmed death and safe-to-restart as different states and adds restart-storm, PID-reuse and cooperative-cancellation cases.
decision_analysis: The watchdog should report a compact anomaly and evidence references without changing plan state. A cached observation cursor can support deduplication, but a status query must not resume work or rewrite completion state. Healthy checks should emit little or no data and never call a model.

A runner can be silent while blocked on I/O or waiting for a provider. Process death, stale lease, missing session output and no semantic progress are different evidence. Only an owned dead runner with runnable work and no live job conflict is a restart candidate. Unknown remote liveness is not safe-to-restart.

The keepalive action needs an exclusive generation-fenced lock, a sliding restart budget and backoff. Persist the reason for every refusal and restart attempt. Operator pause/cancel must survive recovery; otherwise a helpful watchdog can repeatedly resurrect work the user deliberately stopped.

An observer model may suggest a diagnostic after deterministic anomaly detection, but it must not become a second autonomous process controller. A stale recommendation must expire with the observed generation. Cancellation-acknowledgement rules of native agents also apply before replacing their workers.
ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
